data.title: Nevus spilus (speckled lentiginous nevus) — viva
data.summary: Nevi & hamartomas · 5 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Nevus spilus (speckled lentiginous nevus)** (Nevi & hamartomas)_

**Q1. What is nevus spilus?**
- Speckled lentiginous naevus: a light-brown café-au-lait-like background patch studded with darker brown-black macules or papules (lentigines, junctional/compound naevi, sometimes blue or Spitz naevi); present at birth or appearing in childhood; considered a type of congenital melanocytic naevus (HRAS/BRAF mosaic)

**Q2. Clinical types.**
- Macular type (flat speckles — lentigines/junctional naevi) and papular type (raised speckles — compound/dermal naevi)
- Size from small to giant/segmental (zosteriform)
- Phacomatosis pigmentokeratotica (papular nevus spilus + nevus sebaceous — HRAS), phacomatosis pigmentovascularis (with vascular malformation), speckled lentiginous naevus syndrome (neurological anomalies)

**Q3. Malignant potential.**
- Low; melanoma reported especially in large/giant or segmental lesions and the papular type — monitor speckles for change; biopsy atypical components

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Café-au-lait macule with lentigines (NF1/Legius — axillary freckling), agminated lentigines/naevi, congenital melanocytic naevus, Becker's naevus, partial unilateral lentiginosis, LEOPARD/Noonan

**Q5. Management.**
- Observation with photographs and dermoscopy; excision of any atypical speckle
- Cosmetic: Q-switched/picosecond lasers (background and speckles), excision of small lesions; caution — laser may complicate monitoring

## Quick spotter facts
- Café-au-lait patch with dark speckles — nevus spilus

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Melanocytic naevi). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
